messages:
Leah: heads-up — customer reported intermittent TLS timeouts when they whitelist our egress IPs but route through their corporate proxy. error shows 'TLS handshake reset'. they suspect proxy hairpinning. any quick guidance?
Sam: is this the tenant that SNATs back to their own egress IP range (hairpin NAT)? that pattern breaks a bunch of proxies/load-balancers.
Devin: could also be TLS-inspect + re‑signing. can you ask whether the proxy terminates TLS or just forwards? quick repro they can run: `curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:3128 https://api.redwood-inference.com/health` and capture cert details.
Anil: another common failure: conntrack/symmetric NAT + hairpin -> LB sees client IP from inside and drops because backend expects external SNAT. ask them to tcpdump on the proxy for dst addr 198.51.100.23 (example our egress) and confirm packets actually reach external route. command: `sudo tcpdump -nn -i any host 198.51.100.23 and port 443`.
Leah: they asked whether we can publish hostnames instead of IP ranges (their security only allows IP-based whitelist). what should we tell them?
Devin: explain tradeoffs: hostnames + SNI are ideal (less brittle) but many firewalls/proxies can't do SNI-based allowlisting or will do TLS-inspect which kills cert chain. offer both options and include a small checklist they can run.
Sydney-Sec: security note — if they do TLS inspection we recommend disabling inspection for `*.redwood-inference.com` (pinning/attestation risk). also call out that rotating egress IPs are possible during maintenance; recommend allowing ranges rather than single addresses if they can.
infra-bot: automated: current documented egress for US regions: `198.51.100.0/28`, `203.0.113.8/29`. see Console > Network > Egress IPs for up-to-date list.
Sam: draft checklist to send customer: 1) confirm proxy mode: transparent forward vs TLS-terminating, 2) if hairpin/SNAT, disable hairpin or route via an external NAT, 3) allow SNI passthrough for `*.redwood-inference.com` or whitelist the CIDR blocks above, 4) disable TLS-inspect for our hosts, 5) ensure keepalive timeouts >= 60s and allow 443/80, 6) whitelist healthcheck hostnames `health.redwood-inference.com` (for active checks) and our LB public IPs, 7) if using an outbound proxy, confirm it preserves original destination for CONNECT.
Leah: perfect, i'll send that checklist and ask for tcpdump + curl output. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Devin: if they share pcap we can pair with them — happy to jump on a quick call.
Anil: FYI ops tip: if they can't change proxy behavior, we have an option to serve a special health endpoint on an allowed IP they can hit directly (low velocity). ping me if we should enable per-customer.
Leah: sounds good — i'll include the option as a fallback in the message. closing thread after customer ack.
